A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adjoint-based PDE discovery work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original PDE-recovery simulations, coefficient errors and execution-time comparisons in Section 3 and Appendix B, with additional empirical analyses in Sections 4–6 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v4 retains original simulation results and adds two-dimensional PDE experiments, additional baseline comparisons and noise experiments in Section 3. Appendix F retains empirical hyperparameter studies.

M1.justification: Section 2, Eqs. 3–4, removes the factor 1/(ΔxΔt) from the constraint functional and coefficient gradient while retaining the terminal condition and learning-rate formula. This changes the reported update scaling within the retained forward/adjoint optimization framework; gradient averaging and the candidate-library approach remain.

E1.justification: v4 retains the original PDE cases and adds two-dimensional heat and Burgers’ discovery experiments in Sections 3.1.1–3.1.2. New two-dimensional noise tests extend to 1% and 5%, beyond v3’s controlled-noise maximum of 0.1%, substantially broadening evaluated input conditions.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates against PDE-FIND alone. v4 adds WSINDy and PDE-LEARN as actual comparators for one-dimensional heat, Burgers’, Kuramoto–Sivashinsky and random-walk experiments in Tables 2, 4, 6 and 8.

E3.justification: The stated heat, Burgers’ and KS time-step formulas drop the added 1 from their coefficient-dependent denominators. v4 also explicitly defines multiplicative noise, f*(1+ε), replacing v3’s additive-noise description, and introduces new comparison grids and raw-versus-denoised controls. These are substantive reported protocol changes; retained plots do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 Tables 10–11 add systematic raw-versus-SVD-denoised comparisons for two-dimensional heat and Burgers’ equations at 0.1%, 1% and 5% noise, including failure cases. Existing sparse-time, ill-posedness, incomplete-library and hyperparameter analyses are retained. The one-dimensional denoising illustration in v3 Figure 3 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify execution times averaged over 10 independent runs and standard-deviation error bars in Section 3. v4’s additional mean-plus/minus entries use this existing practice; no new seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive recovered-equation and timing entries for new baselines and two-dimensional experiments. For example, Table 3 reports 44.87 seconds for Adjoint versus 796.83 seconds for PDE-FIND on the (100,100,100) heat grid; Tables 10–11 add noise-dependent coefficients and runtime failures. Existing sparse-heat and Fokker–Planck coefficients remain unchanged in relocated Tables 9 and 7. The additions are not same-setting performance gains over v3.

T1.justification: v4 Appendices A–B add explicit variational and parameter-gradient derivations, and Appendix C introduces an O(h²)+O(Δt) numerical-gradient error analysis. The learning-rate argument changes its gradient-scaling bound from O(h^(-|d|)) to O(h^(1-|d|)), and Section 2 strengthens the smoothness assumption. These extend the earlier mathematical treatment substantially.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same adjoint-based discovery contribution, machine-accuracy claim and large-data efficiency advantage over PDE-FIND. The additional experiments support these retained claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v4 explains that boundary conditions are assumed known and that parameterized boundaries require another constraint. Its discussion explicitly identifies dependence on a predefined symbolic library when prior information is unavailable. New comparison passages also justify retaining PDE-FIND as the strongest tested alternative.

D1.justification: v4 documents the added two-dimensional initial conditions and their parameters in Eqs. 11 and 14. Tables 10–11 specify the noisy-test grid and learning-rate parameters β=0.02 for heat and β=0.01 for Burgers’. Existing hardware, numerical-solver and default-hyperparameter disclosures remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for Weak SINDy, PDE-LEARN, hard thresholding, variational calculus, plasma-model discovery and variational multiscale methods. Related work consolidates PDE-Net and PINN-SR with PDE-LEARN into a shared discussion, while retaining the original adjoint-based research positioning.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: v3’s Appendix B gallery becomes v4 Section 3.1, former Sections 4–6 become Sections 3.2–3.4, and Appendix C becomes Section 3.5. Appendices are reordered around new derivations, related work is consolidated, notation explanations are expanded and acknowledgements are removed.

P2.justification: v4 adds nine tables and two two-dimensional solution figures, removes v3 Figure 3 and relocates many existing figures into the main results section. Typography, author layout, algorithm formatting and table layouts also change substantially. Most existing plots are reused rather than redrawn.

improvement.justification: The raw-versus-SVD-denoised comparisons address a limitation of v3’s controlled-noise experiments, which used denoising throughout, and make robustness easier to assess. Added derivations improve mathematical transparency. The gain is limited by unexplained KS timing differences between Tables 1 and 6 (9.34 versus 79.14 seconds), a two-dimensional Burgers’ formula in Table 1 that conflicts with Eq. 13, and missing configuration details for the added baselines.
